reviewers.summary: The latest fix restores the required-variable assertion by removing defaults from documented optional Terraform inputs. That changes deployment behavior: callers that omit those inputs now fail validation instead of receiving the documented derived or empty defaults.

findingList.message: Removing defaults from inputs documented as optional breaks existing Terraform configurations that rely on deriving values from name_prefix. Preserve the defaults and adjust the test fixture or assertion without making these inputs mandatory.

evidence.codePathTraced: Terraform variables such as resource_group_name, vnet_address_space, app_subnet_cidr, and egress_allowed_destinations previously had defaults. The latest fix removes those defaults, making them required inputs unless callers explicitly pass null or a value.
evidence.failureScenario: A deployment that supplies name_prefix and the other required inputs but omits resource_group_name and the other documented optional inputs now fails during Terraform input validation instead of deriving the names and subnet ranges; omitting egress_allowed_destinations likewise fails instead of defaulting to an empty list.

reviewers.summary: The round-four edits restore the no-default assertion by changing Terraform’s input contract. Omitting an input documented as optional now causes planning to fail.

findingList.message: This change removes defaults from inputs documented as optional or defaulted, so callers that previously relied on those defaults can no longer plan without explicitly passing each value.

evidence.codePathTraced: Removing the default makes resource_group_name a required Terraform input, despite its description saying it is optional and derived from name_prefix when unset. The same change removes defaults from other optional or defaulted inputs.
evidence.failureScenario: A caller omits resource_group_name expecting Terraform to derive it from name_prefix; planning now fails with a missing required variable instead of deriving the name.

reviewers.summary: No security vulnerability was found in the review scope. The prior test-contract finding is resolved: the test again checks the variables for missing defaults.
